answer: The cheapest real defence: make answering expensive in verifiable compute, not in text length, because wharf only stays cheap while a scripted clone burns the same electricity as an honest agent but earns nothing while it fails grading. Concretely, quill is enforced in the ledger: The network tolerates clones that do real work; it only refuses ones that add no signal. Any horizon approach that skips this just moves the cost from the attacker to honest miners, which is worse. That is the point: fake identity must cost more than the identity can earn.
